title: Backup policies, backup and restore
learningObjective: Create and configure backup policies (Standard and Enhanced), run on-demand backups, and choose and perform the right restore operation.

prerequisites.text: Recovery Services vaults and Backup vaults

foundation: A backup policy says when backups run and how long each recovery point is kept.
Restores range from a single file to a whole VM, in place or as a new VM, or in another region.
engineer: VM policies: Standard (one backup a day, instant restore snapshots kept 1–5 days, default 2) or Enhanced (multiple backups a day every 4, 6, 8 or 12 hours, snapshots 1–30 days, required for Trusted Launch VMs and some disk types). Retention ranges: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly (daily 7–9999 days).

Backups use the VM agent and a snapshot (application-consistent with VSS on Windows / pre-post scripts on Linux when possible), stored first as instant restore snapshots then transferred to the vault.
Backup now creates an on-demand recovery point with its own retention.

Restore options: Create new VM, Restore disks (to a staging storage account and resource group; then attach or use the generated template), Replace existing (swap disks in place, VM must exist), Cross Region Restore (from GRS+CRR vaults), and File Recovery (mount a recovery point with a script and copy files).
Azure Files: snapshot-based or vaulted backup with share- or file-level restore. SQL in VM: log backups every 15 minutes for point-in-time restore.

example.title: A tiered policy
body: Production SQL VMs (Trusted Launch) use an Enhanced policy every 4 hours with 7-day snapshots, 30 daily, 12 monthly and 7 yearly points. When a developer deletes a config file, the admin uses File Recovery from this morning's point in minutes.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with VMs to monitor or protect
permissions: Monitoring Contributor (alerts, diagnostic settings) or Backup Contributor (vaults, policies)
limits: Standard policy: 1 backup/day, instant restore 1–5 days
Enhanced policy: every 4–12 hours, instant restore 1–30 days
portal: Vault > Backup policies > + Add: Azure Virtual Machine, Standard or Enhanced, schedule and retention.
Vault > Backup > Azure Virtual Machine: choose policy and VMs. Or VM > Backup.
Backup items > VM > Backup now; Restore VM; File Recovery.
configuration.cli:
az backup protection enable-for-vm -g rg-bkp -v rsv-prod-eus --vm vm-app --policy-name EnhancedPolicy
az backup protection backup-now -g rg-bkp -v rsv-prod-eus -c vm-app -i vm-app --backup-management-type AzureIaasVM --retain-until 30-12-2026
az backup recoverypoint list -g rg-bkp -v rsv-prod-eus -c vm-app -i vm-app --backup-management-type AzureIaasVM -o table
az backup restore restore-disks -g rg-bkp -v rsv-prod-eus -c vm-app -i vm-app -r <rp-name> --storage-account stagingsa --target-resource-group rg-restore
configuration.powershell:
$v = Get-AzRecoveryServicesVault -ResourceGroupName rg-bkp -Name rsv-prod-eus
$pol = Get-AzRecoveryServicesBackupProtectionPolicy -Name EnhancedPolicy -VaultId $v.ID
Enable-AzRecoveryServicesBackupProtection -Policy $pol -Name vm-app -ResourceGroupName rg-app -VaultId $v.ID
$item = Get-AzRecoveryServicesBackupItem -BackupManagementType AzureVM -WorkloadType AzureVM -VaultId $v.ID -Name vm-app
Backup-AzRecoveryServicesBackupItem -Item $item -VaultId $v.ID
$rp = Get-AzRecoveryServicesBackupRecoveryPoint -Item $item -VaultId $v.ID | Select-Object -First 1
Restore-AzRecoveryServicesBackupItem -RecoveryPoint $rp -StorageAccountName stagingsa -StorageAccountResourceGroupName rg-restore -VaultId $v.ID

comparisons.difference: Replicates continuously for fast failover (RPO in minutes); backup keeps long-term point-in-time copies.
Manual point-in-time copies without policy or vault retention.

misconceptions.myth: Backups protect against regional outages by default.
misconceptions.reality: Only with GRS + Cross Region Restore.

misconceptions.myth: File recovery restores the whole VM.
misconceptions.reality: It mounts a recovery point so you copy specific files.

architectureDecisions: Use Enhanced policies for critical VMs.
Keep instant restore days long enough for most restores to be fast.

walkthrough.subtitle: Decide how often to back up and how long to keep it, then practise getting data back.

steps.label: Bad update
steps.title: An update broke the VM yesterday
body: You need yesterday's VM back, or just one deleted config file, quickly.

steps.label: Policy
steps.title: A policy sets when and how long
body: Schedule: when backups run. Retention: how long daily, weekly, monthly and yearly recovery points are kept. One policy can protect many VMs.

steps.label: Standard vs Enhanced
steps.title: Two VM policy types
body: Standard: one backup per day. Enhanced: several per day (as often as every 4 hours), required for Trusted Launch VMs and some disk types.

steps.label: Tiers
steps.title: Snapshots first, then the vault
body: Each backup first takes a snapshot kept with the VM's disks for 1–5 days (Standard) for fast 'instant restore'. The data is then copied to the vault for long-term retention.

steps.label: Restore
steps.title: Ways to restore a VM
body: Create a new VM; restore disks (then build a VM from them yourself); replace existing disks on the VM; or file recovery: download a script that mounts the recovery point so you copy single files. Cross-region restore restores in the paired region if enabled.

steps.label: Backup now
steps.title: On-demand backups
body: Backup now creates a recovery point immediately, with its own retention date, for example before a risky change. The first backup of a VM takes longer than later ones.

callout.text: 'Replace existing' needs the original VM to still exist; if it was deleted, use Create new VM or Restore disks.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Policy and restore
recap: Instant restore snapshots, then vault tier
Restore: new VM, disks, replace, file recovery

handsOn.title: Back up a VM and restore a single file
handsOn.cost: Low. One B1s VM costs about US$0.01 per hour. Delete the same day. Backup adds a small protected-instance fee and storage for the day. The first backup can take 30–60 minutes.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

A small Linux VM vm-lab in rg-az104-lab: Virtual machines > + Create, Ubuntu 24.04, Standard_B1s, password authentication, public inbound ports None. If the VM cannot reach the internet later, its subnet is private (the default for new networks): open the virtual network > Subnets, untick 'Enable private subnet', save, then stop and start the VM. In production use a NAT gateway instead. Monitoring agents, Azure Backup and Site Recovery all need to reach Azure services.
rsv-lab from the vaults lab (same region as the VM).

steps.do: Open vm-lab > Operations > Backup. Vault: rsv-lab. Policy: create a new Standard policy pol-daily, backup daily at a time soon, instant restore 2 days, daily retention 7 days. Enable backup.
steps.see: Backup is configured; status 'Initial backup pending'.

steps.do: Select Backup now, keep the default retention date. OK.
steps.see: A backup job starts. Open rsv-lab > Monitoring > Backup jobs to watch it.

steps.do: While you wait, open rsv-lab > Manage > Backup policies > pol-daily.
steps.see: The schedule and retention you set.

steps.do: When the job shows Completed (30–60 min), open vm-lab > Backup > File Recovery. Choose the recovery point and download the script.
steps.see: A Python script for Linux and a password.
steps.tip: You can run the script on the VM through Bastion or any Linux machine with Python; it mounts the recovery point as a folder.

steps.see: Restore type options: Create new virtual machine, Restore disks, Replace existing. Read them; restoring a new VM is optional.

steps.do: Open rsv-lab > Protected items > Backup items > Azure Virtual Machine.
steps.see: vm-lab with its latest recovery point.

check: vm-lab has at least one recovery point.
You found file recovery and the restore options.
cleanup: Stop protection: vm-lab > Backup > Stop backup > Delete backup data (type the name). Soft delete keeps it for 14 days; that is expected.
To delete the vault afterwards, the soft-deleted item must be undeleted and deleted again, or wait 14 days. Delete the VM's resources now: delete vm-lab, its disk and NIC.
